original_test_intent: Verify that every required PCIe endpoint and intervening link repeatedly enumerates and negotiates its approved generation and width after each defined cold DC power cycle without AER, device, boot, thermal or platform-health regressions.
original_method: Select by row/variant; identify DC as the project-approved cold-power boundary and map the controller plus all target endpoints/root ports/switches/retimers; capture pre-cycle topology, LnkCap/LnkSta, health and preserved logs; drain workloads; execute only the approved number and timing of cold cycles; after every boot wait for explicit readiness and collect complete enumeration/link/error/thermal evidence; stop on the first abnormal cycle and leave the SUT in the approved final state.
manual_activity: An authorized operator approves and controls the cold DC sequence, observes physical/power safety and performs recovery; the agent can collect the defined read-only link and health evidence after each boot.
required_inputs: Unique identity resolution for the duplicate code
Definition of DC cycle, approved power controller/path, off dwell, stabilization interval, cycle count and final power state
PCIe slot/endpoint UUID or serial/BDF and root-port/switch/retimer mapping with required generation/width
Boot/readiness deadline, allowed link retrain/error limits, workload drain, maintenance window and independent console/recovery plan
safety_requirements: Drain active users/jobs and protect writable data before the first cold power interruption
Preserve existing logs and correlate new records by timestamps rather than clearing evidence
Use only the approved out-of-band controller or qualified operator; never guess a PDU outlet or BMC chassis action
Require complete device and link readiness after each cycle before continuing
Abort on boot timeout, missing endpoint, generation/width downgrade, AER/device fault, thermal/power anomaly or unstable service; no automatic cycle retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate composite identity, cycle plan, topology, approval, controller identity and recovery readiness
Collect complete pre/post/per-cycle PCIe, boot, OS/BMC, error and telemetry evidence
Coordinate only an explicitly approved cycle through the named control path after separate execution confirmation
Do not flash firmware, infer overnight count, choose an outlet, clear logs, continue after a failed cycle, retry automatically or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve duplicate-code ownership while preserving both rows
Approve the cycle semantics, topology/link matrix, timing/count/readiness/error oracle and recovery
Review per-cycle evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The repeated-cold-cycle description matches the row, but no executable power command is safe without a named controller and outlet/chassis identity. `lspci` is evidence collection, not the DC stimulus.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: For each explicitly approved cold cycle, use only the named controller/operator procedure; after readiness, collect full `lspci -Dnnvvv` for mapped devices and correlated host/BMC/error telemetry.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source's overnight/720-minute intent and pre/post speed/link verification are preserved; exact count, off/on timing and normal matrix remain pending.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute a bounded, timestamped cold-cycle matrix with a named power boundary and capture per-cycle device/link/readiness/error state for every mapped PCIe path.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines per-cycle identity, readiness, evidence and abort requirements without converting overnight into a guessed count.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A firmware flash result, single final lspci snapshot or host warm reboot cannot prove repeated cold DC retraining.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Cold interruption can lose data and strand the system; management power telemetry alone may not prove that all downstream rails crossed the intended DC boundary.

project_override_considerations: Engineering must define whether DC means chassis soft-off/on, BMC hard reset, PSU output removal or another cold boundary and prove it differs from row 2209 AC removal. The row-2045 firmware case remains separate.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash and separation from row 2045 firmware flash
Approved cycle plan, controller/outlet or chassis identity, timestamps and operator/maintenance approval
Endpoint/slot/BDF/root-port/switch/retimer map with baseline and every-cycle LnkCap/LnkSta generation/width
Every-cycle power transition, boot/readiness time, complete enumeration and service-health evidence
Correlated AER/dmesg/journal/BMC/SEL plus thermal/power state without cleared history

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Wistron-HW-00486-V002 identifies row 2045 PCIe-switch firmware flash and row 2208 DC Cycle - Speed&Link. Composite identity is reliable, but code-only dispatch could perform a critical firmware write instead of the intended repeated power-cycle/link recovery test.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The cold-cycle PCIe-link objective is clear. Exact topology, cycle semantics, controller, count/timing and thresholds are supplyable project inputs; execution stays approval-gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2208 Wistron-HW-00486-V002: assign/approve a unique identity distinct from row 2045 Flash PCIe Switch Firmware; define the DC power boundary and named controller/outlet or chassis path, exact cycle count/off-on-stabilization timing and final state, target endpoint/slot/serial/BDF/root-port/switch/retimer generation-width matrix, boot/readiness deadline, allowable retrain/AER/error/thermal limits, workload drain, maintenance approval, abort and independent-console recovery.

review_improvement: Prevents accidental firmware dispatch, turns undefined overnight cycling into an auditable approval-gated matrix and preserves per-cycle PCIe plus platform-health evidence without erasing logs.
independent_technical_reasoning: DC cycle is ambiguous unless the rail boundary is named; a host reboot or BMC reset may leave downstream PCIe silicon powered and cannot validate cold retraining. A final lspci sample can hide intermittent failures, so enumeration, generation/width and errors must be captured after every cycle. Because the source states overnight but no count, the reviewer cannot infer repetition or dwell. The shared code is safety-critical because its other variant writes PCIe-switch firmware.
